equation_request.abstract: Lazy quantum walks were presented by Andrew M. Childs to prove that the continuous-time quantum walk is a limit of the discrete-time quantum walk [Commun.Math.Phys.294,581-603(2010)]. In this paper, we discuss properties of lazy quantum walks. Our analysis shows that lazy quantum walks have $O(t^{n})$ order of the n-th moment of the corresponding probability distribution, which is the same as that for normal quantum walks. Also, the lazy quantum walk with DFT (Discrete Fourier Transform) coin operator has a similar probability distribution concentrated interval to that of the normal Hadamard quantum walk. Most importantly, we introduce the concepts of occupancy number and occupancy rate to measure the extent to which the walk has a (relatively) high probability at every position in its range. We conclude that lazy quantum walks have a higher occupancy rate than other walks such as normal quantum walks, classical walks and lazy classical walks.

specification.problem: Simulate a lazy discrete-time quantum walk (coin states L,S,R) on a cycle of N=2^n sites with a 3x3 DFT coin, and classically compute position distributions, moments, and occupancy number/rate for comparison with Hadamard, classical and lazy classical walks.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance: n=4 (N=16), coin in 2 qubits with |3> idle, t=1..5 steps (2t+1<N), statevector readout, no measurements. Occupancy number/rate comparison and moment-scaling fit are classical post-processing. Out of scope: analytic derivation of moment orders, the exact DFT-coin limiting density, and the paper's exact occupancy definition and threshold.

symbols.meaning: position, taken as a signed representative mod N
3x3 DFT coin embedded in the 2-qubit coin space, with |3> fixed

equations.label: Lazy walk step
equations.latex: U=S\,(C\otimes I),\quad S=|L\rangle\langle L|\otimes T^{-1}+|S\rangle\langle S|\otimes I+|R\rangle\langle R|\otimes T+|3\rangle\langle 3|\otimes I,\quad T|x\rangle=|x+1 \bmod N\rangle
equations.description: One step of the lazy walk with a stay option; the idle coin state |3> gets no shift (never populated).
equations.justification: The abstract mentions lazy walks with a DFT coin; the specific 2-qubit encoding is a proposed construction.
assumptions: The coin acts as identity on |3>

equations.label: DFT coin
equations.justification: The abstract names a DFT coin; the matrix is the standard DFT. The sign convention and embedding are assumptions.
assumptions: F_3 is not a standard-library gate; it must be built from ordinary gates (for example via decomposition into rotations and controlled gates), or the coin must be replaced by a Hadamard-like 3-state coin. This is unresolved.

equations.label: State and distribution
equations.description: Initial symmetric coin state, evolution, and marginal position distribution.
equations.justification: Symmetric initial state is a proposed choice; the marginal is standard.
assumptions: Initial coin state is symmetric, giving a symmetric distribution only if the coin and shifts respect the symmetry; this is not guaranteed for a DFT coin and must be checked numerically

equations.label: Moments
equations.description: k-th moment, with the claim of O(t^k) growth.
equations.abstract_quote: lazy quantum walks have $O(t^{n})$ order of the n-th moment of the corresponding probability distribution
equations.justification: The abstract states O(t^n) growth for the n-th moment; the log-log slope fit is a proposed test. For k=1 the moment may be zero by symmetry, so use |x|^k or even k.

equations.label: Occupancy number and rate
equations.description: Occupancy number and rate over the reachable range.
equations.justification: The abstract introduces occupancy number and rate but does not define them; this is a guessed definition with a guessed threshold.
assumptions: Threshold 1/(2t+1) is chosen; the paper's may differ

registers.name: pos
registers.role: position on the cycle, little-endian integer encoding, qubits 0..3

specification.initial_state: pos=|0>, coin=(|L>+i|R>)/sqrt2 = (|00>+i|10>)/sqrt2 in coin bits (c1c0). Prepare with H on coin qubit 1, S on it, and a coin-qubit-0 stay in |0>; the coin value then encodes L=0, R=2. No initialize.

steps.description: Prepare the initial coin state with H and S on the coin MSB.

Repeat t times: apply coin C on the coin register, then conditional shifts: a controlled decrement when the coin is |00>, a controlled increment when the coin is |10>, built from multi-controlled X gates (ripple of MCX), nothing for |01>. Ancillas not needed.

Read the statevector (no measurement), marginalise over coin to get P(x,t), then compute moments, a log-log slope fit, the concentration interval, and the occupancy number and rate; compare against a classical simulation of the Hadamard, binomial and lazy classical walks.

specification.classical_postprocessing: From the statevector index = coin*N + pos (coin as the high qubits), sum |amp|^2 over coin to get P(x,t). Map x>=N/2 to x-N. Compute M_k(t), fit slope of log M_k vs log t, find the interval holding most of the probability, and compute Occ and rho for each walk type; classical comparison distributions come from convolution or the Hadamard-walk simulation.
assumptions: n=4 positions, t<=5 so wraparound is absent
3-state DFT coin padded into 2 qubits with an idle 4th state
Occupancy threshold 1/(2t+1) and range |x|<=t are assumed definitions
Total 6 qubits, within the cap if the cap is at least 6
missing_information: Paper's exact lazy walk definition (the coin may be mixed with a laziness parameter instead of a 3-state coin)
Exact occupancy number/rate definition and threshold
Gate decomposition of the 3x3 DFT coin into standard gates
Whether the claim about the interval compares to t/sqrt2 for a specific coin and initial state
